_meta.model: MODELS.SMART; single call + groundedFacts pre-pass (ticket-appeal:{city}:{type}, 14d cache); followup 2000
_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run (npm run check:golden ticket-tackler) — include the DE case. Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200. GUARDS: (1) assessment.verdict and pay_or_contest.recommendation MUST be an exact English token STRONG_REASON_TO_CONTEST|MAY_BE_WORTH_CONTESTING|NOT_ENOUGH_INFORMATION_YET|LITTLE_BASIS_TO_CONTEST|PAYING_MAY_BE_THE_PRACTICAL_CHOICE (5-way, replaced the v2 3-way WORTH_CONTESTING/VERIFY_FIRST/PROBABLY_PAY on 2026-09-15); what_may_matter[].source MUST be exactly citation|user_account|supporting_evidence; evidence_to_get[].urgency MUST be exactly PRESERVE_NOW|BEFORE_DECIDING|BEFORE_FILING (3-tier, replaced the v2 2-tier today/before_filing) — the frontend switches badge colors/labels on all of these; withLanguage would otherwise translate them in 12 langs. (2) NO numeric case-strength score and NO strength enum anywhere (v2 already removed fight_worthiness/strong-moderate-weak; v3 keeps that ban explicit in the prompt itself, not just as an omission). (3) pay_or_contest is now a STRUCTURED decision summary — supports_contesting, supports_paying, key_unresolved_fact (any of the three may be null), and next_step (never null) — replacing v2's single freeform `reasoning` string. recommendation is NOT required to equal the top assessment.verdict (the prompt explicitly says not to repeat it mechanically — pay_or_contest comes after laying out what_may_matter/evidence, so it can reach a more specific conclusion, e.g. top verdict MAY_BE_WORTH_CONTESTING while pay_or_contest still leans PAYING_MAY_BE_THE_PRACTICAL_CHOICE if the review surfaced nothing new). (4) appeal_letter MUST be null when there is no coherent factual basis for one — see weak-case. NEW field appeal_conditional_on: when the letter depends on an unverified fact, names it in one sentence; MUST be null when appeal_letter is null OR when the letter rests only on already-established facts — do not populate it 'just in case'. (5) what_may_matter[].evidence_that_would_help and how_to_file.method_tips are BOTH independently nullable now (v2 had them always-populated) — null is correct when nothing applies or nothing was verified to add; do not backfill either with generic filler to avoid a blank line in the UI (the frontend conditionally hides the line instead). (6) dont_say MUST be null (not an empty array) unless the user's own account/wording could actually hurt their case. (7) how_to_file.where must literally be the fallback sentence ('Check the citation or the issuing agency's official instructions for the current contest procedure and deadline.') when nothing was verified — this exact sentence is prescribed in the system prompt, not paraphrased. (8) The groundedFacts pre-pass query was broadened 2026-09-15 from 4 topics (deadline/filing/stages/grounds) to 6 (+ fee, + enforcement_hours) per the owner's 'verify before advising' directive — still city+type cached, still never blocks the main call (stale-while-revalidate; a cold cache returns unverified, refreshes for the next request). (9) Quote-heavy German input → NO_QUOTE_RULE. (10) Statute sections cited only when certain. DO NOT reverse: the 5-way verdict enum; the 3-tier urgency enum; the structured (non-freeform) pay_or_contest; appeal_letter/appeal_conditional_on nullability; evidence_that_would_help/method_tips nullability; single-call architecture (unchanged from v2 — letter drafting stays coupled to the assessment).

input.ticketText: CITY OF SEATTLE — PARKING INFRACTION NOTICE. Violation: SMC 11.23.180 — Parking in passenger load zone. Date: 07/22/2026 Time: 6:40 PM. Location: 1400 block, E Pine St. Penalty: $47. Respond within 15 days of issue date.
input.whatHappened: The load-zone sign says the restriction runs 'Passenger Load Zone 7AM–6PM'. I parked at 6:40 PM, after the posted end time. The sign is also partially bent behind a tree branch — you can barely read it from the street side.

assessment.reason: According to your account, the sign restricts parking only through 6 PM, and you parked at 6:40 PM — after that posted end time; if the sign actually reads that way, the citation may have been issued outside the restriction's effective hours. The sign wording has not been independently verified, so confirming what it actually says is the essential next step.

what_may_matter.fact: Citation time is 6:40 PM; user says the sign reads 'Passenger Load Zone 7AM–6PM'
what_may_matter.why_it_matters: If the restriction ended at 6 PM, a 6:40 PM citation would fall outside the posted enforcement window and could be a basis for dismissal.
what_may_matter.needs_verification: The exact wording on the sign has not been independently confirmed — only the user's reading of it is on record.
what_may_matter.evidence_that_would_help: A clear photograph of the sign showing the full posted hours, taken while legible and before the sign is repaired or replaced.

what_may_matter.fact: User says the sign is partially bent and obscured by a tree branch, making it barely readable from the street
what_may_matter.why_it_matters: If the sign's hours are difficult to read from the street, this may be relevant to whether the restriction was adequately posted.
what_may_matter.needs_verification: Whether Seattle's municipal code or enforcement rules require that a load zone sign be clearly legible from the street in order to be enforceable.
what_may_matter.evidence_that_would_help: Photographs from the driver's street-level viewpoint showing the obstruction, and a check of Seattle's sign visibility or posting requirements.

what_may_matter.fact: Citation cites SMC 11.23.180 — Parking in passenger load zone
what_may_matter.why_it_matters: The specific code section would govern what hours and conditions make parking a violation.
what_may_matter.needs_verification: The actual text of SMC 11.23.180, including whether it sets any time-of-day conditions independent of posted signage.
what_may_matter.evidence_that_would_help: The text of SMC 11.23.180 from the Seattle Municipal Code, available at the City of Seattle's official code website.

what_to_verify: The exact hours posted on the sign at 1400 block E Pine St — confirm whether it reads '7AM–6PM' or something different.
The text of SMC 11.23.180 — specifically whether the violation depends on posted sign hours or has a fixed statutory schedule.
The official contest procedure and deadline from the citation or Seattle Municipal Court's parking infraction instructions.

evidence_to_get.item: Clear photograph of the full sign at 1400 block E Pine St showing posted hours
evidence_to_get.why: Establishes what the sign actually says, which is the central fact in dispute.

evidence_to_get.item: Photograph from the driver's street-level viewpoint showing the branch obscuring the sign
evidence_to_get.why: Documents the visibility condition at the time of the citation.

evidence_to_get.item: Photograph of the citation notice itself, front and back
evidence_to_get.why: Preserves all citation details needed for any filing.

input.ticketText:
Stadt Schwäbisch Gmünd – Verwarnung
Tatvorwurf: Überschreiten der zulässigen Höchstparkdauer um 30 Minuten
Ort: Ledergasse, Bewohnerparkzone B
Verwarnungsgeld: 25,00 EUR
Zahlungsfrist: 1 Woche
input.whatHappened: Also, ich hab das Knöllchen an der Ledergasse bekommen. Der Kontrolleur meinte nur „Ihr Ausweis war nicht lesbar“ und ich hab gesagt „Der liegt doch da vorne!“. Mein Anwohnerparkausweis lag sichtbar auf dem Armaturenbrett, war aber wohl beim Türzuschlagen etwas verrutscht, sodass man ihn schräg von oben trotzdem sehen konnte. Angeblich hätte ich die Höchstparkdauer um 30 Minuten überschritten – aber als Anwohner mit Ausweis gilt die doch gar nicht für mich? Ich hab ein Foto vom Armaturenbrett mit dem Ausweis gemacht, direkt nachdem ich das Knöllchen gefunden hab.

assessment.reason: Als Inhaber eines Anwohnerparkausweises für Zone B gilt die Höchstparkdauer laut Ihrer Schilderung nicht für Sie, und Sie haben ein Foto, das den Ausweis auf dem Armaturenbrett zeigt — dies wurde jedoch nicht unabhängig bestätigt.

what_may_matter.fact: Nutzer besitzt einen Anwohnerparkausweis für Zone B
what_may_matter.why_it_matters: Wenn Anwohner mit gültigem Ausweis von der Höchstparkdauer ausgenommen sind, träfe der Tatvorwurf nicht zu.
what_may_matter.needs_verification: Ob die Zonenregelung für Bewohnerparkzone B Anwohner tatsächlich vollständig von der Höchstparkdauer ausnimmt.
what_may_matter.evidence_that_would_help: Der Wortlaut der Zonenregelung, sowie eine Kopie des Ausweises mit Gültigkeitsdauer und Kennzeichen.

what_may_matter.fact: Foto zeigt den Ausweis sichtbar auf dem Armaturenbrett, unmittelbar nach dem Knöllchen aufgenommen
what_may_matter.why_it_matters: Belegt, dass der Ausweis ausgelegt war, auch wenn er verrutscht war.
what_may_matter.needs_verification: Ob das Foto den Zustand zum Kontrollzeitpunkt widerspiegelt.

what_to_verify: Der genaue Wortlaut der Zonenregelung für Bewohnerparkzone B.
Die formale Widerspruchsfrist und das zuständige Amt.

evidence_to_get.item: Foto vom Armaturenbrett mit Ausweis sichern (Original mit Zeitstempel)
evidence_to_get.why: Belegt, dass der Ausweis sichtbar ausgelegt war.

output.appeal_letter:

Stadt Schwäbisch Gmünd
Rechts- und Ordnungsamt / Bußgeldstelle

[YOUR NAME]

how_to_file.where: Check the citation or the issuing agency's official instructions for the current contest procedure and deadline.
how_to_file.deadline_note: Das Verwarnungsgeld ist laut Ticket binnen einer Woche fällig — prüfen Sie das genaue Ausstellungsdatum auf dem Knöllchen.

pay_or_contest.supports_contesting: Ein gültiger Anwohnerparkausweis für dieselbe Zone ist ein konkreter sachlicher Punkt, kein vager Einwand.
pay_or_contest.supports_paying: Ob die Zonenregelung Anwohner tatsächlich vollständig ausnimmt, wurde nicht unabhängig bestätigt.
pay_or_contest.key_unresolved_fact: Der genaue Wortlaut der Zonenregelung für Bewohnerparkzone B.
pay_or_contest.next_step: Den Wortlaut der Zonenregelung prüfen, dann über den Widerspruch entscheiden.

input.ticketText: CITY OF AUSTIN — PARKING CITATION. Violation: Blocking fire hydrant, within 15 feet. Date: 09/02/2026 Time: 2:15 PM. Location: 600 Congress Ave. Fine: $150. Pay or contest within 21 days.
input.whatHappened: I parked in front of a fire hydrant for about ten minutes to grab coffee. I know it's a fire hydrant — there's no ambiguity there. I just didn't think anyone would notice that fast.

assessment.reason: By your own account, you knowingly parked in front of a fire hydrant; you have identified no factual inaccuracy in the citation and no defense against it, leaving no concrete basis to contest.

what_may_matter.fact: You parked in front of a fire hydrant and acknowledge doing so
what_may_matter.why_it_matters: A contest typically requires a factual or procedural error in the citation — your account confirms the underlying violation.
what_may_matter.needs_verification: Nothing further — this is established by your own account

what_may_matter.fact: The citation states the violation as being within 15 feet of a fire hydrant
what_may_matter.why_it_matters: If you were actually parked more than 15 feet from the hydrant, that would be a factual discrepancy worth raising — but your account does not suggest this.
what_may_matter.needs_verification: Whether your vehicle was actually within 15 feet of the hydrant, if you have any reason to believe otherwise.
what_may_matter.evidence_that_would_help: A photo showing the distance between your vehicle and the hydrant, taken at or near the time of the citation.

what_to_verify: Confirm that your vehicle's license plate and description on the citation match your actual vehicle — a mismatch would be a factual error worth raising.

evidence_to_get.item: Full text of the citation, including vehicle description and plate number
evidence_to_get.why: A factual error identifying the wrong vehicle would be a concrete ground to contest.

how_to_file.where: Check the citation or the issuing agency's official instructions for the current contest procedure and deadline.
how_to_file.deadline_note: The citation states you must pay or contest within 21 days of 09/02/2026 — confirm this deadline on the citation itself before relying on it.

pay_or_contest.supports_contesting: If the citation contains a factual error — wrong vehicle, wrong location, or your vehicle was actually beyond 15 feet of the hydrant — that would provide a concrete basis to contest.
pay_or_contest.supports_paying: You acknowledge knowingly parking in front of a fire hydrant, which is precisely the conduct the citation describes, leaving no factual dispute on the core violation.
pay_or_contest.key_unresolved_fact: Whether the citation correctly identifies your vehicle — a mismatch would be the only factual error your account leaves open.
pay_or_contest.next_step: Read the full citation carefully to confirm it correctly identifies your vehicle and plate number; if everything matches, paying is the straightforward path.

dont_say: Avoid saying 'I was only there for ten minutes' as a defense — duration of parking is not a factor in a fire hydrant violation.

input.ticketText:
CITY OF CHICAGO - DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE
AUTOMATED RED LIGHT CAMERA VIOLATION
Location: Western Ave & Peterson Ave
Date: 07/18/2026 9:42 PM
Violation: Disobeying a red light
Penalty: $100.00
Two photographs and video available online
input.whatHappened: I got a red light camera ticket at Western and Peterson. Here's the thing - I entered the intersection on yellow, I was already past the stop line and mid-intersection when it flipped to red. The yellow felt really short at that intersection, like it barely gave me time to react at 35mph. The photos show my car in the middle of the intersection. $100 seems steep for this. Worth fighting?

assessment.reason: Entering on yellow and being mid-intersection when the light turned red does not, by itself, contest what the camera measures — but it's worth checking whether an officer separately issued a paper citation for the same incident, which some cities treat as grounds for dismissal, before deciding to pay.

what_to_verify: Whether a Chicago Police officer issued a separate, hand-written traffic citation for this same incident — if one exists, it may be grounds for dismissal under the city's own camera-violation rules.
What the two photographs and video actually show — specifically whether your vehicle had already crossed the stop line before or after the signal turned red.

evidence_to_get.item: Review the two photos and video available online using the citation number
evidence_to_get.why: Establishes, from the city's own evidence, whether your vehicle crossed the stop line before or after the light turned red.

evidence_to_get.item: Check your records for any hand-written police citation from the night of 07/18/2026
evidence_to_get.why: A duplicate citation for the same incident is a distinct, checkable fact that could change the answer entirely.

how_to_file.where: Check the citation or the issuing agency's official instructions for the current contest procedure and deadline.
how_to_file.deadline_note: Citations of this kind typically state a response window from the Notice of Violation date — confirm the exact deadline printed on your notice before doing anything else.

pay_or_contest.supports_paying: The argument you have — that you entered on yellow — addresses your own intent, not the fact the camera measures, so it's unlikely to change the outcome on its own.
pay_or_contest.key_unresolved_fact: Whether a duplicate paper citation exists for the same incident, since that's a distinct, checkable fact rather than an interpretation.
pay_or_contest.next_step: Check for a duplicate paper citation before deciding whether to pay or contest.

dont_say: Avoid leading with 'the yellow felt too short' — this describes your reaction to the signal timing, not a fact the citation or a hearing officer can act on.

input.question: What if I just don't pay it?
input.analysisContext: PAYING_MAY_BE_THE_PRACTICAL_CHOICE: user acknowledges knowingly parking in front of a fire hydrant; $150 fine; no factual error identified in the citation.

output.answer: Not paying will not make the ticket go away. Austin sends unpaid parking tickets to collections, adds late fees, and can place a hold on your vehicle registration renewal. For a $150 ticket you've acknowledged you owe, non-payment is the most expensive option available to you.
output.watch_out: A registration hold is a real enforcement mechanism — you won't be able to renew your plates until the debt is resolved.
output.next_step: Pay the $150 through the method listed on the citation before the deadline printed on it.
